Compute $\mu - 2\sigma$ and $\mu + 2\sigma$ and match the interval to one of the standard percentages.

easy.statement_latex: A data set is normally distributed with $\mu = 65$ and $\sigma = 6$. Using only the empirical (68-95-99.7) rule, determine the approximate percent of the data that is above $53$.
hints: Write the cutoff in the form $\mu + k\sigma$ (or $\mu - k\sigma$) to figure out how many standard deviations it is from the mean.
The empirical rule gives central percentages of $68\%$, $95\%$, and $99.7\%$ for $k = 1, 2, 3$; the remaining probability is split evenly between the two tails.

By the empirical rule, $95\%$ of the data lies within $2$ standard deviations of the mean. The remaining probability is split evenly between the upper and lower tails.
Values above $\mu - 2\sigma$ include the central interval plus the upper tail beyond $\mu + 2\sigma$.
Therefore the percent above $53$ is about $97.5\%$.
